title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM `Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id)` and `AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id)`, which employ parameterized queries. No raw SQL or string interpolation is present.

The endpoint fetches a rule by the user‑controlled `rule_id` from the URL and only checks organization membership / team ownership via `can_edit_alert_rule`. It does not verify that the rule belongs to the project identified in the URL, potentially allowing an IDOR (muting any rule in the organization). However, the surrounding `ProjectAlertRulePermission` class may enforce the missing check, which is not visible in this diff, so the flaw is not confirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit check that the fetched rule (or alert rule) is associated with the `project` supplied in the URL (e.g., `if rule.project_id != project.id: return Response(..., status=403)`). Ensure the permission class also validates ownership at the project level.
